entries.title: Relativistic tidal excitation of g- and i-modes in neutron star binaries
entries.abstract: When the gravitational wave frequency of an inspiraling binary matches a normal-mode frequency of a neutron star (NS), the mode can be resonantly excited. The excitation transfers orbital energy to the star and shifts the phase of the emitted gravitational-wave (GW) signal, thereby providing a potential probe of the NS interior. However, estimates of this phase shift in the literature vary by orders of magnitude due to different approximations and formulations used in calculating the tidal coupling strength. We revisit this problem using a fully relativistic scattering formalism, which serves as our benchmark calculation and provides a gauge-invariant mode response together with an effective tidal-mode coupling strength. We calculate the phase shifts induced by the excitation of stratification g-modes, crustal interface i-modes, and hadron-quark interface i-modes, and estimate their detectability with Fisher-matrix forecasts for current and next-generation detectors. In our models, direct g-mode excitation remains below the detection thresholds, even for the strongest stratification considered. Crust-core i-modes at large shear speeds provide the most favorable prospects and crust melting can produce a substantially larger phase shift. Hadron-quark i-modes remain below the next-generation detection thresholds.

entries.title: QPO constraints on the rotating Fan-Wang spacetime
entries.abstract: In this work, we investigate a rotating regular black hole described by the Fan-Wang solution, which arises from nonlinear electrodynamics coupled to gravity. We examine the motion of neutral test particles along circular equatorial orbits and derive the corresponding orbital parameters, including the angular velocity, specific angular momentum, and specific energy. By perturbing these orbits in the radial and vertical directions, we calculate the associated fundamental epicyclic frequencies. We then employ the relativistic precession model to interpret the observed quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs) in terms of these frequencies. We numerically determine the radii of the innermost stable circular orbits and perform Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations to constrain the spacetime parameters. Using observational and theoretical estimates of the black hole mass and spin parameter from the literature, together with theoretically motivated priors on the Fan-Wang parameter, we obtain the best-fit parameter values. The inferred black hole mass, spin parameter, and QPO emission radii are consistent with the corresponding estimates reported in the literature. Furthermore, the dimensionless Fan-Wang parameter satisfies $l/M < 8/27 \approx 0.296$, in agreement with its theoretical upper bound.

entries.title: Properties of Chromium and Manganese in Tycho's SNR with XRISM/Resolve
entries.abstract: The X-ray emission of young supernova remnants gives access to the composition and spatial distribution of elements ejected in supernovae. The emission from the ejecta provides crucial insights into the explosion mechanism, especially for Fe-group elements formed in the innermost layers of the star. The objective of this paper is to provide constraints on the supernova progenitor and explosion mechanism of Tycho's type Ia supernova remnant by studying the properties of Cr and Mn. The unprecedented spectral resolution of XRISM/Resolve allows us to detect significant emission lines of Cr and Mn in different regions of Tycho's supernova remnant, even at small scale, providing a much more precise spatial distribution of Cr and Mn with respect to previous measurements. Significant Cr and Mn emission lines are observed in the Fe bright northeastern-to-southeastern emitting rim, some in the center region, but none in the southern region. The observed mass ratios of Mn/Fe, Cr/Fe and Mn/Cr, are consistent with 1D delayed detonation models of near-Chandrasekhar-mass Type Ia supernovae and 1D pure-detonation models of 1 Msol sub-Chandrasekhar-mass progenitors. In both cases, the observations imply supersolar zero-age main-sequence progenitor metallicities. Overall the best agreement is found for models with a too high metallicity to be realistic for Tycho's location. This points to additional sources of neutronisation such as carbon simmering for Chandrasekhar mass progenitor. For sub-Chandrasekhar mass, double detonation models with a WD mass lower than 1Msol are suggested.

entries.title: A branchless single-precision Voigt approximation for spectral synthesis
entries.abstract: The Voigt function is evaluated repeatedly in spectral synthesis, and several widely used implementations carry an absolute error floor. We construct QLG, a family of branchless, single-precision approximations, separable in the damping parameter $a$. QLG is named for its three ingredients: Lorentzian and Gaussian generators $L$ and $G$, and an envelope $q$ that multiplies every fitted correction and vanishes at both endpoints. The leading Lorentzian wing amplitude is fixed analytically. Three members reach observed maximum full-profile relative errors of $6.5\times10^{-3}$, $9.2\times10^{-4}$, and $7\times10^{-5}$ over $a\in[10^{-9},10^{9}]$ and $|v|\le10^{5}$. Extended-domain and randomized checks support these error levels. For the tested SIU, MOOG, and Humlicek w4 implementations, the relative error instead approaches 100% towards small values of the damping parameter. We compare synthesis-weighted costs on an Apple M1 and an AMD EPYC 9554 using gfortran 15, and propagate errors through solar-dwarf, red-supergiant, and M-dwarf syntheses. The least expensive member costs 0.98-1.05 times as much as the tabulated Synspec kernel on the M1 and 1.11-1.20 times as much on the EPYC, with a maximum flux error smaller by a factor of 3.6. The intermediate member costs less than every tested arithmetic kernel and holds the flux error below $10^{-3}$. The most accurate member costs 1.6-3.0 times less than w4 and gives 3.4-5.0 times smaller maximum flux errors in the tested syntheses.

entries.title: Instantaneous Spectral Bandwidth of Solar Type III Radio Bursts in the Interplanetary Medium
entries.abstract: Magnetic reconnection during solar flares accelerates electron beams that generate type III radio bursts through the plasma emission process. Their instantaneous spectral bandwidth is commonly interpreted as a measure of the spatial extent of the emitting population, yet contributions from viewing angle and radio-wave propagation remain poorly constrained. We investigate bandwidths of 20 type III bursts observed by Parker Solar Probe between 0.15-6.5 MHz. The bandwidth increases with frequency and is consistent with previous measurements up to 100 MHz. For the first time, simultaneous observations from multiple spacecraft show similar bandwidths despite large differences in viewing geometry. We further examine bandwidth contributions from intrinsic emission and propagation effects using numerical and analytical simulations, showing that the beam spatial extent is larger than required to explain observed bandwidths, while the spatial extent of Langmuir wave generation produces electromagnetic emission bandwidths near the observed lower limit. Temporal broadening due to radio-wave scattering can increase the bandwidth by causing emission from different frequencies to overlap in time. This effect depends strongly on turbulence level and becomes increasingly important for faster electron beams and narrower intrinsic emission profiles. The results demonstrate that observed type III bandwidths cannot be interpreted solely in terms of physically emitting regions: the intrinsic emission bandwidth follows the spatial extent of Langmuir wave generation, while propagation-induced temporal broadening provides an additional contribution that can reconcile intrinsic and observed bandwidths. Accounting for radio-wave propagation effects is essential when using type III burst bandwidths to infer the spatial properties of their emitting electron populations.

entries.title: Dual and Binary AGN at Cosmic Dawn: The need for a JWST Program to resolve the merger channel of Early Black Hole Growth
entries.abstract: The discovery with JWST of accreting black holes (BHs) at z=4-9 in numbers far exceeding pre-JWST expectations, many of them overmassive relative to their hosts and linked to the enigmatic Little Red Dots (LRDs), raises the question of how early BHs form and grow. Hierarchical assembly predicts that galaxy mergers drive gas to galactic nuclei and bring BHs together, leaving a direct observational signature: dual AGN at tens of kpc separations and sub-kpc to few-kpc "duets" in post-merger galaxies, which are the progenitors of the low-frequency GW sources targeted by pulsar timing arrays and LISA. JWST has opened the window to study these systems at z>3. However, these early discoveries are very limited number and come from heterogeneous, largely serendipitous samples, so these systems can hardly be used for robust statistical studies. Within the Genesis initiative We propose a uniformly selected census of dual AGN and their hosts from cosmic noon to cosmic dawn, as a science case for the Genesis initiative. Our tiered strategy uses the survey imaging and spectroscopy for candidate selection at no extra cost, followed by NIRSpec IFU confirmation, multi-band NIRCam (and MIRI/ALMA) host characterisation, and multi-epoch revisits. Confirming and characterising about 100 pairs requires of order 1000 hr, well beyond the ceiling of standard TAC programs, and demands multi-cycle continuity. The census will deliver pair fractions as functions of redshift, separation and luminosity, BH masses and mass ratios, host properties and environments, and the empirical anchor needed to turn merger models into realistic LISA rate forecasts.

entries.title: FILOS: a solar Filament Oscillation Simulator
entries.abstract: We introduce FILOS, a solar Filament Oscillation Simulator designed to validate methods for inferring filament dynamics from H-alpha observations. FILOS constructs synthetic filaments from measured spines populated with three-dimensional dipped threads containing hydrostatic plasma. It computes H-alpha optical depth, projects the structure onto the image plane, applies the Global Oscillation Network Group (GONG) instrumental response, and embeds the result in observed GONG background sequences. Independently prescribed damped longitudinal and transverse motions can be imposed; longitudinal periods can also be calculated from thread curvature and prominence height using the pendulum model. In a representative longitudinal experiment, thread periods range from 44.2 to 87.6 min (median 60.8 min). Normalized Lomb-Scargle power maps recover the dominant periodicity and a period-halving signature near equilibrium. Time-distance fitting recovers an onset of 19.53 +/- 0.23 min for a prescribed 20 min and a collective period of 57.71 +/- 0.35 min. Differences from input thread-level values reflect projection, image formation, and progressive dephasing. FILOS also supplies segmentation masks and opacity-weighted plane-of-sky velocity fields, enabling controlled tests of oscillation analysis, observational biases, segmentation, and motion estimation.

entries.title: A comprehensive Sun-as-a-star catalog of interplanetary type-III bursts: Statistics and a framework for stellar exospace weather applications
entries.abstract: Decameter-hectometric (DH) type-III bursts, produced by energetic electron beams escaping into interplanetary (IP) space, are often associated with strong soft X-ray (SXR) flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and solar energetic particle events (SEPEs). With future DH missions being planned, these intense bursts could provide reliable exospace weather event diagnostics, given the lack of direct stellar IP particle and CME probes. We present a catalog of DH type-III bursts associated with 538 out of 734 $\geq$C5-class flares observed by Wind and STEREO spacecraft during 2006-2025. Independent of the SXR flare strength, the occurrence and Sun-as-a-star emission properties of DH type-III bursts distinguish confined flares, CMEs with and without strong IP shocks, and SEPEs. We find that logistic-regression models combining SXR and type-III properties provide more accurate and well-calibrated CME/SEPE occurrence probabilities than a model based only on SXR parameters. Further, a space weather event probability-estimation model based on physically meaningful, scale-free parameters derived from SXR and type-III properties outperforms an SXR parameter-only model. This result presents a way to define solar-calibrated exospace weather prediction models extendable to stellar flares with a range of energy scales but similar underlying physics. We also present a catalog of 26 shock-associated type-III (S-type-III) bursts that appear to start from cotemporal DH type-II bursts and are generally associated with fast halo CMEs and major SEPEs. Our catalogs and the scale-free model form a benchmark for exospace weather studies.

entries.title: Prescription for the rotational and orbital evolution of main-sequence binaries undergoing resonance locking
entries.abstract: In intermediate-mass binary stars, dynamical tides may play an important role in the orbital and rotational evolution of the system. One possible channel for long-term angular-momentum exchange is resonance locking, in which the evolution of the orbital and rotational parameters remains coupled to the evolution of the frequency of a resonantly excited oscillation mode. We aim to develop a simple prescription for describing the orbital and rotational evolution of binary systems undergoing resonance locking, and to assess the range of validity of this prescription. Using the asymptotic formalism for high-order gravity modes, we relate the temporal evolution of mode frequencies to the evolution of the orbital and rotational properties of the binary system. We then compare the resulting prescription with full integrations of the dynamical-tide evolution, including the contribution of multiple forcing frequencies. Depending on the type of resonance locking considered, we identify the regions of parameter space in which locking is expected to be possible in terms of orbital separation and rotation rate. We find that resonance locking is favoured in systems with significant spin-orbit asynchronism. When a locking is maintained, the proposed prescription reproduces the main features of the orbital and rotational evolution obtained from full dynamical-tide integrations, without requiring the explicit computation of the complete forcing-frequency spectrum. If resonance locking occurs, the evolution of the binary system can be described by a relatively simple prescription. Comparison with the observed population of binaries containing gamma-Doradus stars suggests that a significant fraction of the sample lies in regions compatible with the expected location of locked systems. Improved characterisation of these systems is required to distinguish resonance locking from alternative explanations.

entries.title: Magnetic Flux Eruptions in Magnetically Arrested Disks: Magnetic Reconnection and Bubble Expansion
entries.abstract: Using a high-resolution GRMHD simulation of a magnetically arrested disk, we investigate the physical mechanism driving magnetic-flux eruption. The horizon-threading magnetic flux declines mainly in off-equatorial regions, whereas localized hot spots associated with magnetic reconnection appear near the equatorial plane around the onset of flux decline. A non-axisymmetric, magnetically supported low-density structure, which we identify as a magnetic bubble, expands radially and azimuthally within a pre-existing low-density channel in the filamentary accretion flow. Based on these findings, we propose a physical picture linking reconnection, bubble expansion, and horizon magnetic flux decline. The reconnection occurs in the pre-existing low-density channel, and may reconfigure the field and promote bubble expansion. Magnetic-pressure gradients provide broadly distributed outward support for the expansion, while magnetic tension contributes a localized outward force near the equator. Bubble expansion may limit gas replenishment, helping to maintain the low-density region and reduce the total pressure near the equator. This pressure reduction may facilitate equatorward electromagnetic energy transport. In the simulation, the polar electromagnetic energy flux reverses from poleward to equatorward near the onset of the horizon-flux decline. The equatorward transport is concentrated in the bubble sector and carries electromagnetic energy from the off-equatorial magnetosphere to the equatorial region. This energy supply may sustain localized reconnection and plasma heating as the eruption develops.

entries.title: Temporal polarization properties of accretion flows into supermassive black holes: INSANE as an alternative
entries.abstract: Temporal variability and polarization provide unique diagnostics of the magnetic field structure and plasma dynamics in accretion flows around supermassive black holes. We investigate the temporal polarization properties of horizon-scale emission using general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations coupled with polarized general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) for three accretion states: Standard and Normal Evolution (SANE), Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD), and an intermediate regime (INSANE). Fourier polarization-mode decomposition, through the ratio $|β_m|/|β_2|$, shows that MAD produces the most rotationally symmetric EVPA patterns, SANE the most asymmetric, and INSANE lies in between. The multi-scale temporal behaviour of the intensity is investigated using the Continuous Wavelet Transform and Hilbert-Huang Transform. Both methods identify localized oscillatory features associated with magnetic-flux eruption events in the MAD simulations. In the shorter interval examined, INSANE distributes its variability more evenly among several time-scales, while the SANE behaviour depends more strongly on the electron-temperature prescription. To quantify the spectral distribution, we define a fast power fraction $F_{\mathrm{fast},I}$ for periods of 80-200 $M$ within a broad band of 80-1500 $M$. Both methods give the smallest fractions for MAD; the ordering of state medians, INSANE > SANE > MAD, persists when the upper fast-band boundary is varied from 200 to 500 $M$. Our analysis demonstrates that combining polarization morphology with multi-scale temporal analysis provides a useful means of distinguishing magnetization states, supporting INSANE as a distinct observational alternative to conventional MAD/SANE for interpreting horizon-scale observations of M87$^{*}$ and related systems.

entries.title: Cataclysmic Variables from XMM-Newton and eROSITA
entries.abstract: Cataclysmic variables (CVs) are interacting binaries where a white dwarf accretes material from a late-type donor. The most evolved systems, referred to as period-bouncers, host degenerate donors. We present XMM-Newton and eROSITA, which provide complementary views of the CV population. We summarize the capabilities of XMM-Newton for timing and spectroscopic studies, and its ability to characterize accretion geometries, magnetic field strengths, and short-term variability across magnetic/non-magnetic CVs. These data allow studies of individual systems, including magnetic period-bouncers with soft X-ray spectra and faint luminosities that offer insights into the late stages of CV evolution. We then present an overview of eROSITA as the first X-ray all-sky survey in the soft band since ROSAT, and its impact on population studies. The eRASS:4 catalog expands the known X-ray sky and will enable volume-limited samples of CVs, complete up to 500pc for standard CVs and up to 250 pc for period-bouncers. Cross-matching eROSITA detections with optical catalogs produced the largest sample of X-ray-selected CV candidates to date, that will refine X-ray diagnostic diagrams, reassess the demographics of magnetic/non-magnetic systems, and identify new highly evolved CVs. Finally, we describe ongoing searches for unknown systems, including CVs selected through probabilistic cross-matching with Gaia, and period-bouncers identified through a multi-wavelength scorecard. These efforts led to the discovery of new period-bouncers and a promising detached period-bouncer candidate, that could validate alternative models for the evolution of CVs. Together, XMM-Newton and eROSITA provide an unprecedented view into the structure, evolution, and demographics of CVs, with eROSITA laying the groundwork for future studies of compact binary evolution, the Galactic Ridge X-ray emission, and related phenomena.

entries.title: Solar atmospheric gravity wave phase differences: insights from MANCHA simulations and observations
entries.abstract: Phase-difference and coherence diagnostics are widely used to identify gravity waves in the solar atmosphere, but their sensitivity to opacity and radiative-transfer effects remains poorly understood. We investigate the robustness of gravity-wave signatures in velocity and temperature diagnostics and their appearance in spectroscopic observables. We perform k-/omega phase-difference and coherence analyses using three-dimensional radiative hydrodynamic simulations with the MANCHA code. Diagnostics are evaluated at constant geometrical heights and optical depths. Synthetic Fe I 6173 Å profiles provide bisector velocities, continuum intensities, and line-core intensities. We also analyse high-resolution quiet-Sun observations from the 1-m Swedish Solar Telescope (SST). Velocity diagnostics show similar phase differences and coherence at both sampling levels, including those derived from synthetic and observed bisector velocities, indicating their relative insensitivity to the sampling method. In contrast, temperature diagnostics show stronger and more extended gravity-wave signatures at fixed geometrical height. Synthetic continuum and line-core intensities retain these signatures but exhibit phase differences more closely resembling temperature diagnostics at constant optical depth. SST observations show similar qualitative behaviour, despite quantitative differences. Our results demonstrate that Doppler velocity provides a relatively robust diagnostic of gravity-wave phase propagation, whereas temperature and intensity diagnostics are more sensitive to opacity and radiative-transfer effects. Consequently, the latter may introduce biases in estimates of wave propagation speeds and energy fluxes.

entries.title: Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing Analysis (BADMET)
entries.abstract: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) variability is widely recognized as a promising avenue for constraining black hole mass, yet its practical application remains limited. Although the correlation between black hole mass and variability timescale has been extensively investigated, finite observational baselines often lead to systematic underestimation of the timescale, thereby hindering reliable mass estimation for individual sources. To address this limitation, we develop the Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing analysis (BADMET), an extendable framework that provides black hole mass estimates by assimilating multiple mass-related parameters that include variability properties. We show that incorporating the variability timescale improves mass recovery in the simulated sample and enhances agreement with the reference masses in the observed sample, achieving uncertainties of $\lesssim 0.5$ dex even with a single X-ray observation.

entries.title: Low-state X-ray spectra of magnetized neutron stars: Probing accretion regimes in SFXTs
entries.abstract: Supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) are a subclass of high-mass X-ray binaries characterized by prolonged quiescent states, making them ideal sources for studying accretion onto highly magnetized neutron stars (NSs) at low rates. In this work, we present a broadband spectral analysis of three SFXTs: IGR J16418$-$4532, IGR J17544$-$2619, and IGR J11215$-$5952, using archival $XMM-Newton$, NICER, and $ NuSTAR$ observations. Joint spectral fitting of the NICER and $NuSTAR$ data for IGR J16418$-$4532 confirms the presence of a cyclotron resonant scattering feature (CRSF) at $\sim 50$ keV, implying a NS magnetic field strength of $\sim 6\times10^{12}$ G. We detect a cyclotron line at $\sim27$ keV in IGR J17544$-$2619, significantly higher than the previously reported energy of $\sim17$ keV, a difference that may reflect luminosity-dependent changes in the accretion flow. Using a double-Comptonization model, we identify the characteristic two-hump spectral shape in IGR J16418$-$4532 and IGR J17544$-$2619 at luminosities $\lesssim10^{35}$ $\rm erg\,s^{-1}$, indicating that this spectral transition is a universal feature of accreting magnetized NSs independent of the source type. Furthermore, the ratio between the cyclotron line energy and the intersection energy of the two humps in both sources is consistent with the empirical relation established in Be/X-ray binaries, suggesting that the overheated polar cap atmosphere model used to explain X-ray pulsars in low-luminosity states is also applicable to SFXTs. In contrast, IGR J11215$-$5952 shows a smooth single-component spectrum at all flux levels, which indicates a relatively weak magnetic field of the NS.

entries.title: New Historical Guest-Star Candidates from Reassessed Chinese Records: Lunar Occultation of Planets
entries.abstract: Ancient Chinese records of lunar occultations of planets have been used to test planetary theories and investigate long-term changes in Earth's rotation. However, certain records contain identification errors whose origins remain poorly understood; we propose that some of these errors may arise from misidentifying guest stars, such as novae or supernovae, as planets. We analyzed 67 errata on lunar occultations of planets from Liu Ci-Yuan's (2015) monograph using modern ephemerides and the open-source Python package \texttt{occultsky}, publicly available on GitHub. Using recorded dates and dynastic capital coordinates, we constructed observing windows anchored at solar noon and extending by $\pm 1$ day. Each window covered the preceding and recorded nights because the date may be off by one day. For each of the 67 records, we cataloged the apparent right ascension and declination $(α, δ)$ at the midpoint of the Moon's visibility window on each candidate night. The band swept by the lunar disk confines a possible transient to a narrow region a few degrees across; these midpoint coordinates serve as proxies for the implied guest-star positions. The catalog supplies candidate positions rather than identifications, enabling remnant and compact-object searches to test the guest-star hypothesis directly. If associations are established, these records could become dated guest-star candidates, and their dates could anchor remnant ages.

entries.title: Search for UHE photon sources using direction-time clustering algorithms with a BDT particle discriminant
entries.abstract: Direction-time clustering methods for neutral particle searches are motivated by the possibility that ultra-high-energy (UHE) neutral particles are produced during flaring periods of various astrophysical sources. In this scenario, clusters of events correlated in both arrival direction and time would be generated, which, when observed, would indicate a neutral-particle flare, and a non-observation would provide upper limits on fluxes for point-like sources. Focusing on UHE photon searches, an improvement of the sensitivity of direction-time clustering methods by the application of different photon tags, such as the depth of the extensive air shower maximum (X_max), the lateral distribution of the total signal across an array of detectors (S_b), or a cumulative signal trace-based discriminant variable (C_t), is investigated. A Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) is used to combine multiple observables, by which photon tagging is optimized and photon/hadron separation is improved. The number of events required to identify a photon flare is thereby further reduced compared to using individual photon tags, across a range of flare durations. The possibility of extending the known and assumed PeVatron photon sources into the UHE regime by applying these clustering methods to existing and future observatory data is also discussed. The discovery of UHE neutral particles would mark the next milestone in multimessenger astrophysics, by which a new window onto the non-thermal universe would be opened.

entries.title: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- The evolution of the radio-loud AGN fraction-stellar mass relation to $z\sim3$ in the Euclid Deep Field North
entries.abstract: The incidence of radio-loud active galactic nuclei (RLAGN) and their energetic output via AGN feedback are crucial in understanding the evolution of galaxies and the large-scale structure of the Universe. In the local Universe, the incidence of RLAGN has been shown to correlate strongly with host galaxy properties, particularly stellar mass. Using the large-area survey capabilities provided by Euclid and the LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR), we present the first study of the RLAGN incidence--stellar mass relation to $z=3.0$. We perform a stringent analysis accounting for cross-matching reliability and stellar-mass incompleteness. In addition, we test the robustness of our results against AGN and host galaxy classification. This yields a sample of $3\,154$ RLAGN in the Euclid Deep Field North, comprising $2\,803$ low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs). We find that the LERG incidence as a function of stellar mass and radio luminosity follows a tight correlation over more than two orders of magnitude in stellar mass to $z=3.0$. The slope of the power-law relation decreases from $γ\approx2.5$ in the local Universe to $γ\approx1.0$ at $z=3.0$, indicating a relative increase in low-mass LERGs at earlier epochs. Separating the LERG population into actively star-forming and quiescent galaxies reveals that quiescent LERGs show a much steeper relation between incidence and stellar mass, with $γ\approx2.5$ compared to star-forming LERGs that show $γ\approx1.5$. However, the relation seems to be independent of whether galaxies are star-forming or quiescent at $z\geq2$, where both populations show relatively flat relations with $γ\approx1.0$. Our results suggest an evolutionary picture in which the LERG population transitions from cold-mode, merger-dominated accretion at earlier epochs to a scenario in which systems require a massive hot halo to fuel the AGN in the local Universe.

entries.title: A novel method for dust evolution in protoplanetary disks and a new criterion for gap opening
entries.abstract: We present the Grain Residence-Time Method (GRTM), a computationally efficient particle-tracking approach for studying dust evolution and trapping in protoplanetary disks. By reconstructing steady-state dust distributions from particle residence times, this method provides a way to obtain radial dust surface density profiles without directly evolving the dust as a fluid. We compare the GRTM with dust profiles computed via standard methods using the $\texttt{FARGO3D}$ code, which models the dust as a pressureless fluid, and find very good agreement over a wide range of parameter space. Finally, we investigate how dust gap formation depends on the planet-to-star mass ratio ($q$) and Stokes number ($\mathrm{St}$), through a parameter study, establishing an empirical criterion for dust gap opening. In doing so, we have discovered a new regime of gap opening for small grains with $St \lesssim 10^{-2}$ and for planet mass well below Jupiter's, which is likely very relevant for gaps seen in ALMA images.

entries.title: FastSpecFit: Spectrophotometric Modeling of 38 Million Extragalactic Targets from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Second Data Release
entries.abstract: Optical spectrophotometry provides a direct window into the physical conditions, kinematics, and formation histories of galaxies and quasars. FastSpecFit is an open-source Python software package that forward-models each Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectrum jointly with its broadband photometry, convolving stellar-population synthesis and emission-line templates with each fiber's native spectral resolution. This forward-modeling approach preserves DESI's uncorrelated pixel statistics, fits a typical spectrum in ~0.1 s of single-core time, and scales to tens of millions of objects, with uncertainties estimated via Monte Carlo resampling. FastSpecFit measures stellar velocity dispersions, non-parametric star-formation histories, stellar masses, star-formation rates, dust attenuation, K-corrections, rest-frame magnitudes, and fluxes and equivalent widths for 46 emission lines, including separate narrow and broad components for the Balmer lines. We describe these algorithms in detail, validate the measurements against independent codes, and present the resulting value-added catalog for DESI Data Release 2, which provides spectrophotometric and physical properties for 38 million extragalactic targets at 0<z<4. We also release a companion photometry-only catalog and document the catalogs previously released for the DESI Early Data Release and Data Release 1.

entries.title: Probing the Macroscopic Imprints of Singularity Resolution: Polarization Diagnostics of Rotating ABG Black Holes
entries.abstract: Recent observations by the Event Horizon Telescope have revealed important electromagnetic information around the supermassive black holes $\text{M87}^*$ and $\text{Sgr A}^*$, providing experimental supports for investigating physics near the event horizon. In the absence of a complete quantum gravity theory, exploring the observational appearances and polarized images of accretion flows in regularized geometries, and seeking specific observational differences from Kerr black holes, is of value for understanding the singularity problem. Based on backward ray tracing method, this work investigates both the optical and polarimetric observational features of rotating Ayón-Beato-García spacetime with regularization parameter $Q$. It is found that, compared with the Kerr case, the parameter $Q$ leads to a significant contraction of the size of the inner shadow in the observed optical images. This contraction remains visible even after an illustrative Gaussian filter for images observed at a low inclination angle (e.g. $17^\circ$). In the polarized images, we focus on two observables, the electric vector position angles (EVPAs) and the depolarization regions, on the observer's screen. It is found that depolarization regions do not necessarily reside in the vicinity of the bright photon ring in images at high inclination angles (e.g. $83^\circ$), and a multi-branch structure can be observed. Furthermore, the distribution of EVPAs is insensitive to the regularization parameter $Q$ while the morphology of the depolarization regions can be impacted remarkably by $Q$. The results provide possible optical observable characteristics for the rotating regular spacetime.

entries.title: Observational diagnostics of external photoevaporation at millimetre wavelengths
entries.abstract: External photoevaporation is increasingly recognised as an important influence on protoplanetary disk evolution. However, there are no established molecular line diagnostics that can reliably distinguish external irradiation from variations in intrinsic stellar and disk properties. We use a large grid of thermochemical models to predict the fluxes of 48 transitions from eight species observable with ALMA, spanning a wide range of system properties and external FUV fields of 100 to 100,000 G0. At fixed stellar and disk properties, all transitions generally brighten with increasing FUV field strength. HCO+ and CO fluxes increase monotonically in virtually all disks, whereas lower-excitation lines, particularly those of C2H and N2H+, respond weakly and non-monotonically. However, variations in stellar mass and disk size introduce substantial degeneracies, limiting the usefulness of individual line fluxes as tracers of external irradiation. We therefore assess all pairwise line flux ratios, which can significantly reduce these degeneracies, evaluating their correlation with the external field, the magnitude of their change across the FUV range, and predicted ALMA detectability. We identify 135 promising ratios, including several combining strong FUV sensitivity and high detectability with efficient single-tuning ALMA observations. The strongest diagnostics either contrast high- and low-excitation lines of the same or co-spatial species (e.g. CO J=8-7/J=1-0), probing different regions of the photoevaporative wind, or pair an FUV-sensitive wind tracer with comparatively insensitive emission arising closer to the disk (e.g. HCO+ J=3-2/C2H N=3-2). Our results provide a framework for identifying externally photoevaporating systems from spatially unresolved emission and constraining their incident FUV field strengths.

entries.title: \texttt{StochAXtic}: a JAX-Accelerated, End-to-End Differentiable Framework for Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds from Compact Binary Populations
entries.abstract: We present \texttt{StochAXtic}, a package for computing the dimensionless energy density spectrum $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ of the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by compact binary coalescences. Rather than sampling binary populations via Monte Carlo, \texttt{StochAXtic} exploits the \emph{scale invariance} of the waveforms: at fixed mass ratio, spins and tidal deformabilities, the waveform depends on the total mass only through the dimensionless combination $Mf$. This allows all computationally expensive waveform evaluations using \texttt{LALSuite} to be performed once and stored in a population-independent lookup table. The subsequent integrals over mass and redshift can then be recast as convolutions and evaluated efficiently using fast Fourier transforms. We further employ truncated singular value decomposition to compress the lookup table, reducing both computational cost and memory requirements. Once the table has been computed and cached, \texttt{StochAXtic} evaluates $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ in a few milliseconds, achieving a relative numerical error below $10^{-3}$ at frequencies up to $1$ kHz. Its results agree with those of \texttt{popstock} within the latter's statistical uncertainties. Implemented entirely in \texttt{JAX}, \texttt{StochAXtic} also provides gradients of $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ with respect to population hyperparameters, enabling its direct integration with gradient-based inference methods including Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.

entries.title: The low-luminosity state of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205
entries.abstract: Context. At low accretion rates, X-ray pulsars can develop a two-hump spectrum through the thermalization and Comptonization of cyclotron photons in an accretion-heated, strongly magnetized atmosphere. Sources with independently measured cyclotron-line energies, $E_{\rm cyc}$, are particularly important because they provide a direct estimate of magnetic field strength and allow the continuum shape to be tested against spectral formation models. Aims. We investigate the luminosity-dependent spectral evolution of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205 and constrain the accretion regime in its newly observed low-luminosity state. Methods. We analyzed three NuSTAR observations obtained during the 2023 and 2025 outbursts, corresponding to the high-, intermediate-, and low-luminosity states at $L_{3-79}\simeq5\times10^{36}$, $4\times10^{35}$, and $6\times10^{34}$ erg s$^{-1}$, respectively. We supplemented these data with Swift/XRT observations and performed broadband spectral analysis of all three states. Results. The high-luminosity spectrum follows a classical cutoff power law, whereas the intermediate- and low-luminosity spectra require two thermal Comptonization components to reproduce their two-hump shape. In the intermediate state, the cyclotron line, first reported at $\sim50$ keV in the high-luminosity state, lies on top of the high-energy hump. We interpret the low-luminosity state as representing stable accretion from a cold disk. IGR J06074+2205 thus joins the very limited sample of X-ray pulsars with cyclotron-line energies that have been observed with a double-humped spectral shape.

entries.title: The long-period central star of planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455
entries.abstract: A significant fraction of planetary nebulae have been shown to host short-period binary central stars, but longer period central stars are scarcer. We aim to characterise the central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455 which has previously been claimed to be an intermediate-period binary with a period of approximately 12 days. We study archival and catalogue photometry to probe the previously reported photometric variability and binary spectral energy distribution. We use long-term high-resolution spectroscopic monitoring to measure the radial velocity curves of the two components of the central binary, as well as derive their atmospheric parameters. We also undertook kinematical and chemical abundance analyses of the nebula itself. We find that the central binary of MPAJ1508-6455 has an orbital period of more than five years with a large eccentricity. The binary comprises a relatively low temperature sdO-type central star and a spun-up K-type giant companion. The Kiel mass of the central star is approximately half the dynamical mass derived from the radial velocities. While the nebular systemic velocity and inclination are consistent with the radial velocities of the binary, the nebular abundance pattern adds support for a lower mass progenitor which did not experience hot bottom burning (and is thus more consistent with the Kiel mass than the mass derived from the radial velocities). To the best of our knowledge, the central star of MPAJ1508-6455 is only the fourth planetary nebula central star to have a spectroscopically confirmed orbital period longer than one year.

entries.title: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
entries.abstract: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=α\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $α$ by construction, whereas increasing $α$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$α_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density. The transition pressure and the energy-density jump grow monotonically with $α$, both scale \RB{approximately} with the available-volume fraction $q=1-κ$, and the Seidov onset-instability diagnostic stays below unity.

entries.title: An Efficient Method for Directly Integrating the Vlasov Equation in Collisionless and Weakly-Collisional Simulations
entries.abstract: We describe and test a new numerical method to solve the Vlasov/Boltzmann equation in systems with arbitrary levels of collisionality. The method combines recent ideas to evolve the distribution function (DF) directly in 6+1 dimensional phase-space in a manner which is Lagrangian in both position+velocity. The 'particles' of traditional Monte-Carlo/Particle-In-Cell/N-body (MC/PIC/NB) methods become mesh-generating points defining a volume partition, each of which carries a set of momentum-Lagrangian basis functions representing a local anisotropic momentum DF. The DF is then integrated between cells and bases via a higher-order reconstruction and Godunov-type method, evolving a 10 or 13-moment representation of each basis to ensure manifest mass/momentum/energy conservation. The method allows one to represent arbitrary DFs, including multiple independent streams but also collisional or phase-mixed or thermal distributions (unlike traditional 'moments' or waterbag/tessellation methods), and the cost is bounded to a modest multiplier of MC/PIC/NB costs. We provide an example implementation which uses a spatially-Lagrangian volume partition, second-order reconstruction, and simple set of bases which ensure constant cell masses and couple directly to existing MC/PIC/NB machinery, made public in the code GIZMO. We validate in a series of test problems, demonstrating manifest conservation, Galilean and translation and rotation invariance, and ability to represent complex DFs without spurious dissipation or instability. We discuss applications where this method can have advantages compared to traditional algorithms for simulations of dark matter, stellar, weakly-collisional neutral gas, and particulate/dust dynamics; multiphase/polydisperse flows; cosmic ray and radiation transport/hydrodynamics; and plasma physics.

entries.title: Convergence of the quasinormal-mode expansion of the Kerr Green function
entries.abstract: Black-hole ringdown is usually modeled as a linear superposition of quasinormal modes, and fits to gravitational-wave observations increasingly include high overtones. However, the overtone sum does not necessarily converge: overtones are more strongly damped and thus decay faster in time, but their amplitudes in the Green function (the signal at an observer produced by an impulse at a source point) grow, so the mode description may break down before a finite time. We show that for a rotating (Kerr) black hole this time has a clear geometric meaning. For highly damped modes, the amplitudes grow exponentially with the optical distance from the source and the observer to a characteristic "bounce" radius close to the black hole, defined as the location where the mode amplitude is smallest. For one family of modes, the amplitudes are also suppressed the farther the source and observer sit from the equatorial plane. Rotation therefore makes the onset of convergence depend on direction as well as distance, extending the geometric picture from bounce radii to bounce surfaces. Combining these effects gives a sufficient condition for absolute convergence. For spin $a/M = 0.7$, we map how this time varies with source and observer position, and amplitudes computed numerically reproduce the predicted spatial dependence to better than one percent. These results set geometric limits on when the quasinormal-mode sums converge.

entries.title: oMEGACat-JWST I.: Project description and photometric data release
entries.abstract: Omega Centauri (NGC 5139, $ω$ Cen) is the most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way and the likely stripped nucleus of an accreted dwarf galaxy. Extensive HST observations have uncovered many of its peculiar features, including complex subpopulations and kinematic evidence for an intermediate-mass black hole via central fast-moving stars. High-precision astrometric follow-up is essential to constrain the orbits of these stars. We present oMEGACat-JWST, a deep photometric and astrometric catalog of $ω$ Cen's core and surroundings that extends our previous oMEGACat efforts to near-infrared wavelengths. The superior sensitivity and angular resolution of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) provide significant astrometric and photometric improvements, particularly for faint stars. Our catalog is based on a custom reduction of NIRCam and NIRISS imaging across three JWST programs extending out to two half-light radii (10'). In total, our catalog contains approximately 677 000 sources. In the region overlapping with oMEGACat, we achieve high relative completeness (> 90% of HST sources recovered) while detecting over 86 000 new sources below HST's detection limit. Astrometric tests demonstrate a single-image precision as good as 0.5% of a NIRCam pixel (0.15 mas) at mF115W=18; at mF115W=23 the precision is still 1 mas. Color-magnitude diagrams based on our data show the well-known split between the primordial Helium and the Helium enriched populations and are particularly sensitive to light-element (CNO) variations of faint stars. oMEGACat-JWST provides the most complete photometric catalog of $ω$ Cen's core to date. Combined with HST data, it enables multi-wavelength subpopulation analyses. Together with future monitoring observations, its high astrometric precision will improve our understanding of the kinematics of the central fast-moving stars in $ω$ Cen.

analysis.reason: This work presents the largest early-time ($\delta t \lesssim 2\ \mathrm{weeks}$) HST UV spectroscopic sample of young core-collapse supernovae to date, establishing decisive constraints on shock breakout cooling, progenitor radii, and circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction.
analysis.result: Most standard SNe II are consistent with low-density circumstellar medium (CSM) environments characterized by mass-loss rate $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{M_\odot\ yr^{-1}}$, wind velocity $v_w \approx 50\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, and standard explosion kinetic energy $E_k = (0.6\text{--}1.2)\times 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}$. Discrepancies in early UV continuum brightness indicate progenitor initial radii larger than standard models ($R_* > 500\ \mathrm{R_\odot}$). In contrast, SNe with confined dense CSM require substantially enhanced mass-loss rates, such as SN 2024faq with $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{M_\odot\ yr^{-1}}$ ($R_{\rm CSM} \approx 2\times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{cm}$) and SN 2023ixf with $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{M_\odot\ yr^{-1}}$ ($R_{\rm CSM} \approx 6\times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{cm}$, $E_k \approx 1.2\times 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}$). Narrow C III $\lambda 2297$ emission traces persistent photoionization at $r > 8\times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{cm}$ ahead of a shock moving at $v_{\rm shock} \approx 10^4\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ with unshocked wind velocity $v_{\rm wind} \approx 25\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$. In addition, UV resonance line transitions have large optical depths ($\tau_{\rm line} \gg 1$) undergoing repeated line-scattering, rendering UV emission intrinsically directional and sensitive to multi-dimensional CSM asymmetry.

analysis.problem: The physical origins of early-time ultraviolet diversity and spectral heterogeneity across young core-collapse supernovae, specifically resolving whether early UV flux and line profiles are governed by RSG progenitor envelope structures, shock cooling, or confined dense circumstellar material (CSM) interaction and geometric asymmetry.
analysis.method: Target of Opportunity (ToO) UV spectroscopy from HST/STIS (G230LB, G430L, G750L spanning $\sim 1600\text{--}10000\ \mathrm{\mathring{A}}$) within $\delta t \lesssim 2\ \mathrm{weeks}$ of first light, combined with Swift/UVOT and ZTF multiband photometry, host extinction correction via Na I D equivalent width $A_V^{\rm host} = (0.78 \pm 0.15)\ \mathrm{mag} \times ({\rm EW}_{\rm NaID}/\mathrm{\mathring{A}})$, and 1D non-LTE radiative transfer modeling using CMFGEN across varying mass-loss rates $\dot{M} = 10^{-6}\text{--}10^{-1}\ \mathrm{M_\odot\ yr^{-1}}$ and explosion energies $E_k = (0.6\text{--}1.2)\times 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}$.

analysis.result: Super-Eddington accretion breaks the spherical limit, yielding logarithmic total disk luminosity scaling $L/L_{\rm Edd} \approx 1 + \ln(\dot{M}/\dot{M}_{\rm Edd})$ due to radial photon advection within the photon trapping radius $R_{\rm tr} = (\dot{M}c^2/L_{\rm Edd})r_g$, with maximum effective temperature $T_{\rm eff,max} \simeq 0.2(M_{\rm BH}/10^5 M_\odot)^{-1/4}\ {\rm keV}$. analysis.reason: This review evaluates theoretical accretion disk instability models for quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs), providing valuable physics-based constraints on emission mechanisms, timescales, and disk geometry relevant to high-energy compact object astrophysics.
analysis.result: Assesses dynamical and thermal-viscous disk instability models: differential Lense–Thirring precession produces disk tearing on nodal precession timescales $\tau_{\rm np} = \frac{1}{2a}\left(\frac{R}{R_g}\right)^3\left(\frac{GM}{c^3}\right)$ matching observed periods $t_{\rm rec} \sim 2\text{--}50\text{ h}$, whereas standard radiation pressure instability (RPI) viscous timescales $t_{\rm visc} \sim \alpha^{-1}\left(\frac{H}{R}\right)^{-2}\Omega_{\rm K}^{-1}$ are orders of magnitude too long unless the disk is severely truncated ($R_{\rm out} \lesssim 15 R_{\rm Schw}$) or stabilized by modified stress $\tau_{r\phi} = \alpha P_{\rm gas}^\mu P_{\rm tot}^{1-\mu}$ and magnetic cooling.
analysis.problem: Investigates whether quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) in repeating extranuclear transients originate from intrinsic accretion disk instabilities (dynamical tearing or radiation-pressure thermal-viscous limit cycles) versus extrinsic orbital or geometrical impact scenarios.
analysis.method: One-dimensional time-dependent accretion disk simulations (GLADIS) and limit-cycle analysis solving entropy balance $\Sigma T \frac{\partial S}{\partial t} = Q^+ - Q^-$ and surface density diffusion $\frac{\partial \Sigma}{\partial t} = C_{\rm thv} k(T, \Sigma)$ with wind mass loss $f_{\rm out} = 1 - \frac{1}{1 + A \dot{m}^2}$, evaluating tearing criteria under bending-wave ($\alpha \lesssim H/R$) and diffusive ($\alpha \gtrsim H/R$) regimes.
assumptions: Accretion disks around spinning low-mass supermassive black holes ($M_{\rm BH} \le 10^7 M_\odot$) have large misalignment angles and small viscosity parameters favoring differential Lense–Thirring tearing.
limits: At present, no single theoretical model provides a fully satisfactory explanation of all observed QPE properties, with tensions remaining in reconciling short recurrence times, burst amplitudes, and long-term period evolution.

analysis.reason: This review comprehensively synthesizes RSG mass-loss rates, the Humphreys-Davidson limit, Type II-P plateau mechanics, and pre-supernova circumstellar medium interaction critical for transient modeling.
analysis.result: RSG steady-wind mass-loss rates are constrained to $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-6}\text{--}10^{-5}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ (insufficient for single-star wind envelope stripping), while flash spectroscopy and early shock-breakout light curves require short-lived pre-explosion rates of $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-4}\text{--}10^{-2}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ producing confined CSM with $M_{\rm CSM} \lesssim 0.1\,M_\odot$.
